The United States, which had remained neutral for almost the entire war, loaned a massive amount of money to Britain and France. Britain and France, in turn, loaned a lot of that money to Russia. At that point, the healthy paper balances collapsed and it took the US economy with it. Part of the reason it took so long to recover was because the Allied nations fought another world war in that time and had to rebuild the global economy to clear those debts through international economic growth rather than simple payments.
